label: Records native: same ELF, wall time versus CPU frequency (controlled, physical Alpha)
question: Is the published Records native 47.8us (revision 1fd89e81, 888f39a9) -> 100.5us (revision 96c23c7d) a compiler regression?
verdict: No. The ELF measured in the 96c23c7d receipt has the same sha256 as in the 1fd89e81 and 888f39a9 receipts (e84cba664053..., 6272 bytes); as do the native ELFs of all six kernels between the 1fd89e81 and 96c23c7d receipts. One unchanged ELF takes 45.4us/call at 4.3 GHz and 240.9us/call at 0.8 GHz on this machine: time x frequency is constant (195.7 us*GHz, 192.7-197.2 over 26 steady unpinned rounds, 0.8-4.3 GHz), so 100.52us corresponds to 1.95 GHz and 47.8us to 4.09 GHz. Direct control: the same revision (96c23c7d) with the same ELF was re-measured on the same Alpha at 21:09:47 and gave 47.75us (teacher receipt c-teacher-alpha-before.json), and revision 36e6caf9 gives 47.18-47.27us.
host: alpha · Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-8700 CPU @ 3.20GHz, 12 CPUs, physical (no virtualization), cpufreq governor powersave (intel_pstate, HWP), a qemu guest keeps the 1-minute load near 3-4

elf.origin: build/wasm-tier/Records.native on Alpha, built 2026-11-16 18:14 from checkout 36e6caf9 plus dirty files by the standard harness (bench/wasm_tier.py wrapper: 32 calls per process, exit status 42 checked)

method: Per sample: one subprocess.run of the ELF (32 Records calls per process, as bench/wasm_tier.py measure() does for native), minimal environment, stdout discarded; 150 ms warmup then 11 samples per round; 30 rounds unpinned and 30 each pinned to cpu 0, 2 and 4 (taskset); scaling_cur_freq of the cpu read before and after each round. One command through Alpha's build-queue.
statistic: per-round median of the 11 batch samples / 32; frequency law fitted on rounds whose frequency stayed within 3% during the round (26 of 30 unpinned)
pinned_note: Pinned to cpu 0, 2 or 4 the same ELF takes 59.0-60.6us/call at 4.3 GHz (257 us*GHz): those logical CPUs share a core with a busy sibling thread (the qemu guest), a second environmental factor.
limitations: The receipts record no CPU frequency, so the implied 1.95 GHz is inferred from the law, not observed.

The old ELFs were not rebuilt: Alpha's checkout holds other lanes' uncommitted work and was not reset; byte identity of the recorded artifact hashes is the evidence that the code did not change between 1fd89e81 and 96c23c7d.
This ELF comes from checkout 36e6caf9 plus dirty files, not from a pushed revision; it shows the law, not a per-revision speed.

same_revision_remeasurements.note: Retained Alpha receipts of the C-teacher lane. c-teacher-alpha-six-before.json is the very run published as wasm-tier-targets-2026-11-16.json (same measured_at, same samples). Revision 96c23c7d with the identical ELF (e84cba664053) measured 100.52us at 19:35:41 and 47.75us at 21:09:47, both on the physical Alpha with the same harness sha256s; revision 36e6caf9 (includes the constructor placement commit e991274a; ELF f0bc11ac9c8e, 2624 bytes) measured 47.18us and 47.27us. Records native therefore did not slow down between 1fd89e81 and 36e6caf9.
